bug_semantics: OPA's HTTP Data API turns the request path into a Rego query by building an ast.Ref (stringPathToRef / stringPathToDataRef) and feeding ref.String() to rego.Query(), which re-parses the string. After d3f5102aa, non-identifier ref terms are emitted as [" + raw path segment + "] with no JSON escaping of quotes. A segment such as foo"];malicious_call();x=[" (URL-encoded foo%22%5D%3Bmalicious_call%28%29%3Bx%3D%5B%22) therefore serializes to a multi-statement query (data["foo"];malicious_call();x=[""]), injecting attacker-controlled Rego. Evaluation cannot exfiltrate arbitrary documents beyond the requested path, but the injected code can force success/failure (oracle / misdirected decisions) or be computationally expensive (DoS). v1.4.0 rejects quote characters in path terms and re-parses the constructed query, requiring a single ref.
flaw_origin: The Data API has constructed evaluation queries from path.String() since 3ebbeede6ce37a3e6db6aac380ba762388121093 (2017), but that round-trip was safe while Ref.String() wrapped non-identifier terms with p.String() (strconv.Quote). d3f5102aa4d60a7f7b037761c5a43ac776359b56 (PR #7172, 2024-11-14) rewrote Ref.String() for allocation reduction and replaced "["+p.String()+"]" with unescaped ["+str+"], first writing the interpolation that lets HTTP path quotes break out of the reconstructed query. That is not a move of already-vulnerable lines: the immediate parent still uses strconv.Quote. GHSA/CVE affected range < 1.4.0 is broader than the regression (BIC is first tagged in v1.0.0; v0.70.0 does not contain it).

reasoning: CVE-2025-46569 / GHSA-6m8w-jc87-6cr7 is a real, published code-injection issue in the standalone OPA Data API: an HTTP path is turned into a Rego query and re-parsed, so a crafted path can inject extra statements. The attack surface lives in server makeRego (and the health-check path) calling rego.Query(stringPathToDataRef(urlPath).String()), but that pattern existed since 2017 and was a safe AST round-trip while Ref.String() used strconv.Quote for bracketed terms. The smallest commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism is d3f5102aa4d60a7f7b037761c5a43ac776359b56, which dropped that quoting while rewriting Ref.String() for fewer allocations. Immediate parent d0dfc041 still uses p.String()/strconv.Quote, so injection is absent there. The 2017 query-from-path change and later server.go moves/refactors (including makeRego) are not BICs. PR #7172 is a single commit with the same tree, so it is not a decomposable squash. The GHSA fix ad206324 (v1.4.0) rejects quotes in path terms and asserts the parsed query is a single ref; that commit is the direct public fix (single parent, fork member not in history).
